arxiv-2205-07638.title: EFX Allocations: Simplifications and Improvements
arxiv-2205-07638.creator: Hannaneh Akrami, Noga Alon, Bhaskar Ray Chaudhury, Jugal Garg, Kurt Mehlhorn, Ruta Mehta
arxiv-2205-07638.description: Abstract The existence of EFX allocations is a fundamental open problem in discrete fair division. Given a set of agents and indivisible goods, the goal is to determine the existence of an allocation where no agent envies another following the removal of any single good from the other agent’s bundle.

arxiv-2304-10191.title: Efficient Uncertainty Estimation in Spiking Neural Networks via MC-dropout
arxiv-2304-10191.creator: Tao Sun, Bojian Yin, Sander Bohté (✉)
arxiv-2304-10191.description: Abstract Spiking neural networks (SNNs) have gained attention as models of sparse and event-driven communication of biological neurons, and as such have shown increasing promise for energy-efficient applications in neuromorphic hardware. As with classical artificial neural networks (ANNs), predictive uncertainties are important for decision making in high-stakes applications, such as autonomous vehicles, medical diagnosis, and high frequency trading.

arxiv-2405-04619.title: Non-anomalous non-invertible symmetries in 1+1D from gapped boundaries of SymTFTs
arxiv-2405-04619.creator: Pavel Putrov, and Rajath Radhakrishnan
arxiv-2405-04619.description: Abstract We study the anomalies of non-invertible symmetries in 1+1D QFTs using gapped boundaries of its SymTFT. We establish the explicit relation between Lagrangian algebras which determine gapped boundaries of the SymTFT, and algebras which determine non-anomalous/gaugeable topological line operators in the 1+1D QFT.

arxiv-2503-15643.title: Schmid-Higgs Mode in the Presence of Pair-Breaking Interactions
arxiv-2503-15643.creator: Maxim Dzero, Alex Kamenev
arxiv-2503-15643.description: Abstract Collective modes in superconductors provided the first realization of the Higgs mechanism. The transverse Goldstone mode acquires a gap (i.e. a mass) when it hybridizes with the electromagnetic gauge field. The longitudinal Schmid-Higgs mode, on the other hand, is always massive.

arxiv-2510-11557.title: Invisible Languages of the LLM Universe
arxiv-2510-11557.creator: Saurabh Khanna 1,2, Xinxu Li 1 1 Amsterdam School of Communication Research, University of Amsterdam 2 Pembroke College, University of Oxford
arxiv-2510-11557.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Saurabh Khanna 1,2, Xinxu Li 1 1 Amsterdam School of Communication Research, University of Amsterdam 2 Pembroke College, University of Oxford. Large Language Models are trained on massive multilingual corpora, yet this abundance masks a profound crisis: of the world’s 7,613 living languages, approximately 2,000 languages with millions of speakers remain effectively invisible in digital ecosystems.

pmc-10520408.title: Management of liver hydatid cyst: A case report
pmc-10520408.creator: Banwari Lal Bairwa, Ayush Anand
pmc-10520408.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Key Clinical MessageHydatid disease, if not properly managed, can lead to mortality. Open surgery is preferred and can be a curative approach for multiple and large liver hydatid cysts. Also, regular follow‐up is required to detect recurrence.Keywords: case report, echinococcosis, hydatid disease, management, surgery

Cystic echinococcosis, also known as hydatid disease, is a zoonotic disease and leads to significant mortality if not adequately managed, particularly in Asia. 1 Patients usually present with upper abdominal discomfort, anorexia, and weight loss.

pmc-10692736.title: Atypical genotoxicity of carcinogenic nickel(II): Linkage to dNTP biosynthesis, DNA-incorporated rNMPs, and impaired repair of TOP1-DNA crosslinks
pmc-10692736.creator: Casey Krawic, Michal W. Luczak, Sophia Valiente, Anatoly Zhitkovich
pmc-10692736.description: Cancer is a genetic disease requiring multiple mutations for its development. However, many carcinogens are DNA-unreactive and nonmutagenic and consequently described as nongenotoxic. One of such carcinogens is nickel, a global environmental pollutant abundantly emitted by burning of coal. We investigated activation of DNA damage responses by Ni and identified this metal as a replication stressor.

pmc-10758603.title: Quo vadis cardiac rehabilitation; the role of comprehensive cardiac rehabilitation in modern cardiology
pmc-10758603.creator: Nenad Lakušić, Ivana Sopek Merkaš
pmc-10758603.description: In accordance with the guidelines established by prominent European and global cardiology associations, comprehensive cardiac rehabilitation (CR) stands as an officially endorsed and highly recommended therapeutic approach (class I recommendations; level of evidence A) for a diverse spectrum of cardiac patients.

pmc-11462008.title: Key targets of signal transduction neural mechanisms in acupuncture treatment of cardiovascular diseases: Hypothalamus and autonomic nervous system
pmc-11462008.creator: Xiang Zhou, Jie Zhou, Fan Zhang, Qi Shu, Yan Wu, Hui-min Chang, Bin Zhang, Rong-lin Cai, Qing Yu
pmc-11462008.description: BackgroundCardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death worldwide. As a traditional Chinese treatment method, acupuncture has a unique role in restoring the balance of the human body environment. Due to its safety, non-invasive nature, and effectiveness in treating cardiovascular diseases, acupuncture has been widely welcomed and recognized among the world.

pmc-11508670.title: The Effect of Hive Type on Colony Homeostasis and Performance in the Honey Bee (Apis mellifera)
pmc-11508670.creator: Rola Kutby, Barbara Baer-Imhoof, Samuel Robinson, Lucy Porter, Boris Baer
pmc-11508670.description: Simple SummaryWe provided honey bees (Apis mellifera) with two different hive setups and compared the bees’ ability to maintain colony homeostasis. We conducted a field experiment in a Mediterranean climate covering the period when honey bees were most active, including the dry and hot summer months.

pmc-11570084.title: The Inflammatory Characteristics of Symptomatic Glioma Associated With Poor Prognosis and Chemoresistance via Tumor Necrosis Factor Signaling Pathway
pmc-11570084.creator: Jeongman Park, Dongkil Kim, JeongMin Sim, Yu Jin Kim, Kyunggi Cho, Ju Hyung Moon, Kyoung Su Sung, Jihwan Yoo, Jaejoon Lim
pmc-11570084.description: BackgroundAmong gliomas, the most common primary malignant brain tumor, incidental gliomas account for 2.5%–5% of cases. The controversy over whether to pursue immediate treatment or adopt a wait-and-see approach remains, and more molecular and immunological evidence is needed for definitive treatment decisions.

pmc-11629025.title: Changes in Functional Connectivity Relate to Modulation of Cognitive Control by Subthalamic Stimulation
pmc-11629025.creator: Johannes Achtzehn, Friederike Grospietsch, Alexandra Horn, Christopher Güttler, Andreas Horn, Ana Luísa de Almeida Marcelino, Gregor Wenzel, Gerd‐Helge Schneider, Wolf‐Julian Neumann, Andrea A Kühn
pmc-11629025.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Subthalamic (STN) deep brain stimulation (DBS) in Parkinson's disease (PD) patients not only improves kinematic parameters of movement but also modulates cognitive control in the motor and non‐motor domain, especially in situations of high conflict. The objective of this study was to investigate the relationship between DBS‐induced changes in functional connectivity at rest and modulation of response‐ and movement inhibition by STN‐DBS in a visuomotor task involving high conflict.

pmc-12436868.title: Optimizing Psychopharmacotherapy in Special Populations: Educating Language Models for Tailored Treatment Approaches
pmc-12436868.creator: G Vannini
pmc-12436868.description: AbstractIn recent years, artificial intelligence has increasingly demonstrated its potential to transform healthcare, particularly in the domain of psychopharmacotherapy. This workshop explores the integration of language models into the personalization of treatment strategies for special populations, including those with complex comorbidities or unique pharmacokinetic profiles.

pmc-12448775.title: Trouble de type dyskinésie tardive d’apparition rapide après une dose unique d’halopéridol
pmc-12448775.creator: Carolyn Michelle Tan, Barbara Liu, David Juurlink
pmc-12448775.description: l’apparition précoce de la dyskinésie tardive. L’âge avancé est le principal facteur de risque en ce qui concerne l’incidence et l’apparition précoce de la dyskinésie tardive. On n’a établi aucune durée d’exposition minimale à un antagoniste dopaminergique permettant de distinguer la dyskinésie tardive d’un trouble de type dyskinésie tardive chez les personnes âgées.

pmc-12470488.title: Luthrodes pandava Larvae Can Distinguish Cycas Leaf Quality in Cafeteria Experiments
pmc-12470488.creator: Thomas E. Marler
pmc-12470488.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryThe butterfly Luthrodes pandava is a widespread invasive species that produces larvae that feed on immature leaves of Cycas species. Since Cycas taxa are members of the group of plants known as cycads, and this plant group is the most threatened plant group that has been assessed, a greater understanding of the interactions between the host and the herbivore is needed. I evaluated the ability of L. pandava larvae to preferentially feed on leaves from high quality Cycas species.

pmc-12566765.title: Legacy Building from the Perspective of Palliative Care Professionals in Portugal: A Qualitative Thematic Analysis
pmc-12566765.creator: Carlos Laranjeira, Andréa Marques, Ana Fátima Fernandes, Maria Aparecida Domingos, Isabel Borges Moreira, Richard Gray
pmc-12566765.description: Background/Objectives: Legacy planning should respect te care preferences of people facing serious illness and integrate palliative care (PC). Legacy creation with the guidance of health professionals in PC assumes a therapeutic nature and aims to respond to the psychospiritual needs of patients and their families. To date, research on professional experiences to create legacy in PC remains scarce.

pmc-12668353.title: Exploring the therapeutic potential of epsom salt bath on pain and intensity of knee osteoarthritis: Randomized controlled trial
pmc-12668353.creator: Vijay Kumar, Rajesh Shyoran, Bharat Pareek, Rimple Pathania, Ria Ranaut, Ramya Kundayi Ravi
pmc-12668353.description: BACKGROUND:Osteoarthritis is significantly linked to aging and heavy physical occupational activity, which is a necessary part of many people’s daily lives, and Epsom salt baths are extremely popular among knee pain sufferers. The study aimed to compare the effectiveness of Epsom salt baths in preventing pain and improving activity of daily living among elderly people with knee osteoarthritis.

pmc-13158178.title: Follow-up Strategies in Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: Current strategies and Challenges
pmc-13158178.creator: Sung Gon Kim, Sang Eok Lee, Dae Sung Yoon, In Seok Choi, Ju Ik Moon, Nak Song Sung, Seong Uk Kwon, In Eui Bae, Seung Jae Roh, Min Kyu Kim, Ran Song, Hee Jin Yeon, Youngjin Kim
pmc-13158178.description: Metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) is an effective treatment for severe obesity and its related comorbidities. However, the long-term success and safety of these procedures depend heavily on continuous postoperative follow-up. Postoperative follow-up during the first year is essential for detecting surgical complications, monitoring weight loss trajectories, and optimizing nutritional status.

pmc-13605982.title: Disparity and Inequity of Elementary School Children’s Vision Health and Basic Clinic Resources in Rural and Urban Areas in Taiwan
pmc-13605982.creator: Jui-Yu Lin, Fu-Gong Lin, Rouh-Mei Hu, Jung-Kai Tseng
pmc-13605982.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Among 10,610 Taiwanese elementary school children, myopia and measurable astigmatism were highly prevalent. Myopia prevalence was generally higher in the upper grades. Children living in rural and especially or extremely remote areas had better uncorrected visual acuity than those living in urban areas.

pmc-13630911.title: Multiple stark juckende erythrosquamöse Plaques
pmc-13630911.creator: Lea-Isabell Präger, Marie Rabe, Manfred Kunz, Pietro Nenoff, J C Simon
pmc-13630911.description: Wir berichten über eine 26-jährige schwangere Patientin, die sich mehrfach notfallmäßig aufgrund von stark juckenden Hautbefunden in unserer Klinik vorstellte. Auch der Partner und ihre 2 Kinder waren von ähnlichen Hautveränderungen betroffen. In der mykologischen Diagnostik konnte Trichophyton indotineae nachgewiesen werden. Dieser Erreger breitet sich ausgehend vom indischen Subkontinent auch in Europa zunehmend aus.

pmc-13642943.title: Repurposing the HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor atorvastatin for SRD5A3-congenital disorder of glycosylation
pmc-13642943.creator: Hiba Daghar, Seul Kee Byeon, Claudia Maios, Jennifer Poon, James Doyle, Wasantha Ranatunga, Éric Samarut, Ethan O. Perlstein, Eva Morava, Akhilesh Pandey, J. Alex Parker, Kristin A. Kantautas
pmc-13642943.description: BackgroundSteroid 5 alpha-reductase 3-related congenital disorder of glycosylation (SRD5A3-CDG) is a rare inherited disease characterized by neurological dysfunction, including ataxia, as well as developmental and visual impairments, with no approved treatments. The disease is caused by defects in dolichol biosynthesis, a pathway essential for protein glycosylation.
